=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Package (SPA-N-001 to SPA-N-016)

**Scope note:** I've reviewed all 16 items. The Seller's "[STANDARD]" labels, "cleared" status, and "reviewer efficiency" note don't limit this review, and I haven't treated the Seller's "FINAL" or "market" assertions as established. I haven't seen the full SPA, so clause references come from the Seller's summary and may not match the drafting. Legal points on NSW law and Australian privacy and tax should be confirmed by the deal team before they go into the mark-up.

**Time-critical:** DD-006 (the export incident) may trigger a 30-day eligible data breach assessment under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Part IIIC, if the Seller or Company is an APP entity or otherwise covered. That window may already have run since the disclosure date of 22 September 2026. Confirm the assessment status with the Seller now.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4.8M, for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer should want:** A higher general cap, around 30% (AUD 7.2M), with fundamental and tax claims capped at the full price. Specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, incident) should sit outside the general cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 30% for general warranties, with fundamentals and tax at 100%. The known issues in the disclosure letter already run to roughly AUD 4.1M (Riverlark AUD 3.2M, Sandbar AUD 0.33M, bonuses AUD 0.42M, Ironquay AUD 0.18M) before any incident or revenue loss, so a 20% cap leaves little room for general warranty recovery.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis (about 0.10%). A deductible AUD 250k basket (about 1.04%), so only the excess above the basket is recoverable.
- **Buyer should want:** A low de minimis, a tipping basket (once exceeded, recovery runs from the first dollar), claims aggregated with related claims treated as one.
- **Recommendation:** Counter with a AUD 10k de minimis and a tipping basket of about AUD 120k (0.5%). A deductible basket means the first AUD 250k of loss falls on the buyer, which is a large share of likely warranty losses in a SaaS business.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Any limitation applies to all claims.
- **Buyer should want:** 36 months for general warranties. Tax claims run to the ATO amendment period plus about 6 months. Fundamental claims run for the full limitation period (6 years under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW) for contract, subject to deed/other analysis).
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "one limitation for all claims" approach. Revenue, change-control, and privacy issues often surface after 18 months, and an audit cycle may not have closed by then.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (capacity, authority, title to shares, solvency) capped at 100% of price, with no de minimis, no basket, no disclosure defence, no buyer-knowledge defence, and a 6-year period.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title is the buyer's most basic protection, and it should not be subject to the same thresholds as ordinary warranties.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Not expressly addressed. Clauses 9.3, 12.8, and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy, and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer should want:** An express carve-out so that fraud (by the Seller, its associates, or the Company's management) is outside all caps, time limits, thresholds, disclosure defences, and non-reliance language.
- **Recommendation:** Add an express fraud carve-out. As drafted, the Seller's wording could be read to cover fraud, and courts generally won't enforce contractual exclusion of fraud liability, but an express carve-out avoids the argument.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Clause 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room as at 22 September 2026. Clause 1.2 discloses the Accounts, statutory registers, and public records. Schedule 7 relies on general disclosure.
- **Buyer should want:** General data-room disclosure deleted. Disclosure must be specific, fairly disclosed, and against a specific warranty. Accounts disclosure limited to identified items.
- **Recommendation:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Clause 1.1 would deem the buyer to know everything in a large data room, which would largely hollow out the warranty package.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer should want:** A pro-sandbagging clause: buyer rights are unaffected by knowledge, except for matters specifically disclosed in the disclosure letter.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Combined with 1.1, this would defeat warranty claims on the very issues the buyer has already identified in diligence. The buyer's known issues should be handled through specific indemnities or price adjustment, not through a knowledge bar.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (about AUD 3.6M). The Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. No final consent or evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** A condition precedent to Completion requiring a final written consent in agreed form, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied. Walk-away right if not obtained, or a price adjustment or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** Make Bluefen consent a non-waivable CP. "Reasonable endeavours" is not a condition. Any consent must actually satisfy the conditions in 11.3, not merely exist.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2M outstanding. To be addressed by a release "following Completion." The data room has no final discharge of security.
- **Buyer should want:** Repayment at Completion from the sale proceeds in the funds flow (consistent with debt-free/cash-free), a payoff letter, and a discharge of security (including a PPSR discharge) delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Require payoff and discharge at Completion, not after. A post-Completion release leaves the buyer owning a company subject to bank security and a secured debt it has not priced.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** Conditional Completion bonuses of AUD 420k. Not in the draft funds flow. The disclosure doesn't say whether payroll tax, superannuation, or on-costs apply.
- **Buyer should want:** Bonuses and all related on-costs treated as seller-borne debt-like items, deducted from price, or paid by the seller outside the Company. A specific indemnity for any unpaid bonus, payroll tax, super guarantee, or related on-costs.
- **Recommendation:** Treat the bonuses as debt-like and deduct them from the price. For a rough sense of exposure, superannuation guarantee at 12% on AUD 420k is about AUD 50k, and NSW payroll tax (verify current rate and threshold) may add more.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment. The AUD 180k is open, and the IP transfer under clause 7.3 is conditional on payment. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Payment of the SOW3 balance before Completion at the seller's cost, a confirmatory assignment of SOW3 Project Materials, an IP ownership warranty, and an uncapped specific indemnity covering IP ownership defects and third-party claims, outside the basket and with an extended time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "adequate." The indemnity should cover IP ownership, not just the payment, and the IP transfer should be a Completion deliverable.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** Preliminary matter, "not expected to be material." DD-006 records a download link sent to an unintended external address; the export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). Whether unauthorised access occurred, the scope, and whether notification is required are all unresolved.
- **Buyer should want:** An independent forensic investigation before Completion, a privacy impact and notifiable data breach assessment, and a specific indemnity (outside cap and basket, with extended time) covering investigation costs, notification costs, regulator action, and third-party claims. Consider an escrow or retention.
- **Recommendation:** Reject "not expected to be material." The Seller's own disclosure says the investigation is preliminary and the scope is unknown. The specific indemnity and escrow should stay until the NDB assessment is complete.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals at AUD 110k each (AUD 330k aggregate), described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Copies of the three contracts, confirmation of term, termination rights, and whether they are in working capital. Any commitment beyond Completion that is not ordinary course should be seller-borne or deducted.
- **Recommendation:** Verify before accepting "ordinary course." Read together, the three renewals at the same value need an explanation of why they are separate and whether they were structured to stay under a threshold.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** A single regime for all claims (cap, basket, time limit, knowledge bar, disclosure).
- **Buyer should want:** Separate regimes for: (a) general warranties; (b) fundamental warranties (capacity, title, authority, solvency); (c) tax; (d) IP; (e) specific indemnities (bonuses, Riverlark, Ironquay, incident); and (f) fraud. Each with its own cap, threshold, and time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single regime. The risk profile differs across these categories, and a single regime makes the weakest protections apply to the most important ones.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012 showing Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100%.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: a current ASIC company extract, inspection of the original register and share certificates, confirmation of no transfers, options, or encumbrances (including a PPSR search), and a board resolution approving the sale. A fundamental title warranty.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the register alone as evidence of title. Commission ASIC and PPSR searches and check the share transfer chain before signing.

### SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime above."
- **Buyer should want:** A specific pre-Completion tax indemnity (including payroll tax, super, GST, PAYG, and any tax on the bonuses), with a time limit tied to the ATO amendment period. IP as a separate category with an ownership warranty and a longer time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. The general regime is not appropriate for tax or IP, and the Ironquay and bonus issues make these categories especially exposed.

---

**Priority for the mark-up:** (1) Bluefen CP and Riverlark payoff at Completion; (2) specific indemnities for incident, Ironquay, and bonuses, outside the general regime; (3) delete general data-room disclosure and the buyer-knowledge bar; (4) category separation with fundamental and tax at the full price; (5) fraud carve-out; (6) threshold and time-limit counter-offers; (7) title verification.
